radiusSource: Radius 1.05 +/- 0.01 Jupiter radii and temperature 275 +/- 5 K from evolutionary models at the planet's dynamical mass, age and measured luminosity, Sanghi et al. orbitalPeriodSource: Derived: Kepler's third law with the sample's semi-major axis 15.755 au and total mass 0.7956 solar masses, 70.1 years of 365.25 d. Sanghi et al. (2026, AJ; arXiv:2603.08787): the Octofitter fit of their fiducial model to three decades of radial velocities with a Gaussian-process activity model, Hipparcos-Gaia absolute astrometry and JWST/MIRI, JWST/NIRCam and VLT/VISIR relative astrometry, whose posterior of 32,768 samples they publish on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.19931118, epsInd_allData_obspri-post.fits). Picked with tools/objects/hosted-orbits/posterior-pick.py (src/objects/eps-indi-ab/source/orbits/pick.json): highest logpost (-1258.85) of 32,768 samples.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray. No image, colour, map or oblateness of Epsilon Indi Ab is measured; only its size, mass and orbit are.

semiMajorAxisSource: The recorded orbit's semi-major axis, 15.75 au, from the sample of highest log-posterior in the published posterior of Sanghi et al. (2026, arXiv:2603.08787) (packages/astronomy/data/bodies/eps-indi-ab.json).
massSource: Dynamical mass 6.5 +0.7/-0.6 Jupiter masses from radial velocities, Hipparcos-Gaia astrometry and imaging, Sanghi et al. (2026, arXiv:2603.08787), Abstract.
